note: Text-to-video prompts for the video benchmark. Original to this repository. Kept small and fixed so a run is reproducible; a clip is far slower than an image, so the set is short. The categories are chosen to separate what video models differ on: whether things move plausibly, whether the camera obeys, and whether a simple physical scene holds together over time.

categories.motion: A subject that must move across the shot, not just twitch.
categories.camera: A specified camera move the model has to actually perform.
categories.physics: Water, smoke or cloth that must behave plausibly over the clip.
categories.scene: An establishing shot where the environment, not a subject, carries the motion.

prompts.prompt: A single brown horse galloping left to right across a flat green field, legs moving in a correct gait, dust kicked up behind the hooves, camera tracking alongside at a constant distance, overcast afternoon light.
A slow smooth camera orbit around a small stone lighthouse on a rocky headland, the sea behind it, the light in the tower rotating once, late golden hour, the horizon staying level throughout.

Close-up of dark tea being poured from a ceramic pot into a small glass cup, a steady stream that narrows as the cup fills, gentle steam rising, the surface rippling, a warm kitchen background slightly out of focus.

A wide fixed shot of a stormy coastline, large waves breaking against black rocks, sea spray thrown into the air, low grey clouds moving quickly inland, grass on the clifftop bending in the wind, no people.
